approaches.name: Plain recursion
approaches.intuition: `ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2)` written directly. It recomputes the same subproblems over and over.
steps: Base cases: 1 way for step 0 and 1
approaches.time: O(2^n): far too slow for large n

approaches.name: Rolling two values
approaches.intuition: Each answer depends only on the previous two, so keep just those two numbers and walk up to `n`.
steps: Start with 1 way for step 0 and step 1
Replace the pair with `(b, a + b)`
pitfalls: The result grows quickly: use a 64-bit integer (the statement guarantees it fits).

talkTrackMd: Define the subproblem (ways to reach step k), write the recurrence, point out it is Fibonacci, then collapse the table to two variables.
